motion.name: landing-master-timeline
motion.value: Paused Anime.js timeline; five 1000ms chapters; connected route travel, track reveals and a pivoting junction
motion.purpose: Native scroll seeks one paused Anime.js timeline across five 1000ms windows. Connect draws the rails through four source checkpoints. Trace carries one commit through the original build, passing tests and release. Understand opens the reproduction branch. Investigate draws the return track toward the related code. Automate pivots the junction tongue before moving the evidence into human review. The routes share their endpoints; the carrier follows curve distance and aligns to the route tangent, including elevation. There is no idle rotation. Checkpoint labels move into a compact logo row when branches open. GLSL reveals the rails, shades their beveled metal and highlights the active route. Reverse scrolling retraces the same journey. Frame-rate-independent damping uses 1 - exp(-delta * 10), with delta capped at 0.05 seconds. Rendering stops at rest, outside the story and in hidden tabs. DPR caps are 1.6 desktop and 1.25 mobile. ResizeObserver tracks the renderer and story so source-preview height changes preserve chapter synchronization.

motion.name: landing-workflow-playback
motion.value: User-initiated Anime.js animation; 2400ms; linear; four selected steps
motion.purpose: Illustrative forward delivery and reverse investigation update tool explanations. The play button disables during playback; reduced motion selects the terminal step.

motion.name: landing-text-sequence
motion.value: Anime.js out(4); headings 340ms, 35ms line stagger; simultaneous supporting copy 320ms
motion.purpose: Landing headings reveal by line with Anime.js out(4): 340ms motion, 35ms between lines, 14px vertical travel and direction-specific horizontal offsets. Supporting explanations start simultaneously and finish in 320ms with a small positional and clipping reveal. Initial opacity remains at least 0.85; there is no delayed word-by-word fade. Understand resolves a 1px blur. A passage can replay after fully leaving the viewport. Completion, exit, focus and hidden tabs finish the active sequence and restore styles. Reduced motion keeps static text; cleanup reverts timelines and observers.

motion.name: landing-static-fallback
motion.value: Labeled static SVG track; reduced motion skips WebGL
motion.purpose: Server-rendered text, code, native links and a labeled static SVG track remain available without JavaScript. Reduced motion skips WebGL initialization; unavailable WebGL, shader failure and context loss reveal the same fallback. Context restoration resumes rendering. Preference changes and unmount dispose geometry, materials, instance resources, observers, listeners, timelines and the WebGL context. Native checkpoint buttons have source-specific names and pressed states; invisible checkpoints are inert. The canvas is decorative. The page retains its keyboard-visible skip link.

narrative.overview:
Forge uses neutral charcoal surfaces, fine gray rules, compact controls, and readable operational detail. The approved dark developer-tool brief is the visual authority. Color communicates state; typography and spacing establish hierarchy.

This document records the implemented Phase 1 foundation in `apps/web`: the overview at `/app`, system status, and setup guide. Authentication, integrations, metrics, charts, and form fields are not implemented and have no established application component conventions here.

The public landing page at `/` follows one illustrative checkout commit along a dimensional delivery track. Two metallic rails draw through GitHub, Actions, JUnit and Sentry checkpoints. A coral carrier follows the track into production, a reproduction branch, a return route to the code and a switched route to human review. Each chapter retains its realistic code preview and fast Anime.js text reveal. The Anime.js palette remains warm charcoal, off-white, coral controls and warm stone integrations. The application retains its compact neutral foundation. The wordmark remains; a future 3D logo is deferred.
keyCharacteristics: Flat charcoal surfaces with subtle borders.
Geist interface text with system monospace for commands and versions.
Restrained controls and explicit, text-supported service states.
Responsive navigation and locally scrollable technical content.
A scoped public landing with a continuous delivery track, tool checkpoints and five code examples.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use state colors with a label and icon. An unverified or loading check must remain visually distinct from a healthy check.

dos: **Do** use subtle borders and tonal separation for operational surfaces.
**Do** pair state color with explicit text and an icon.
**Do** preserve unknown, checking, unavailable, and healthy as distinct states.
**Do** keep mobile technical content locally scrollable with a visible cue when needed.
**Do** use real navigation targets and neutral descriptions of health checks.
**Do** scope the warm charcoal and coral page palette, source colors, display typography, track shaders and checkpoint transitions to the public marketing surface.
**Do** keep the static delivery track, chapter content, and native navigation available with reduced motion, JavaScript disabled, or unavailable WebGL.
donts: **Don't** fabricate metrics, customer data, connected sources, or working planned controls.
**Don't** replace the restrained application foundation with the landing's material gradients, depth, or oversized display text.
**Don't** treat a healthy installation as evidence that an engineering source is connected.
**Don't** document future forms, charts, or authentication screens as implemented patterns.
